richSourceOverview: Original IM 2021 G5 U05:L07 Round Doubloons: understand measurement precision and which underlying thousandth-decimal weights ROUND to same nearest tenth/hundredth/whole reading. A scale's displayed value may be rounded; saying a rounded measurement equals the exact object weight is false.

Warm-up Notice and Wonder A Digital Scale uses credited source image by Bjwebb (public domain Wikimedia), not independently reproduced; teacher shows actual original scale reading before pupils decide which historical coin could be on it. Do not invent the displayed digits from an uninspected figure.

Activity 1 Gold Doubloons: original source historical gold coin printed before1728 mass6.867 grams, after1728 mass6.766 grams. To nearest TENTH, 6.9g versus6.8g, distinguishable; to nearest WHOLE gram BOTH=7g, indistinguishable by a gram-only display; to nearest HUNDREDTH6.87g versus6.77g. Before1728 coin is heavier (6.867>6.766). Source asks pupils to place original two masses on number lines and explain which hundredth marks they approach.

Activity 2 Exact or Approximate? Source 14 pencils on desk is an exact discrete count, Los Angeles population12,400,000 is an estimated large quantity, school-to-park2.4 miles is an approximate length, runner time19.78 seconds is a measurement rounded to hundredths of a second, not a logically exact elapsed time to infinitely fine precision. Teacher reviews how precision affects labels and why not all printed digits imply exactness.
